question: How long is a statement on origin valid under the EU-UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement?
expected: 12 months from the date it was made out, or longer if the importing Party provides so, up to a maximum of 24 months (Article 56(3)).
answer: Under the EU-UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement, a statement on origin is valid for 12 months from the date it was made out, unless a Party decides to extend the period up to 24 months. This is specified in Article 56(3) of the Agreement [a7547bfef8-0022]. However, the UK has chosen to provide for a longer period of up to 24 months for imports into the UK of EU-origin goods [36b53d745c-0040]. The validity period applies to imports into the EU, where the EU is the importing Party, and is limited to 12 months [36b53d745c-0039]. The Commission does not provide information on third country policies, but the UK has extended the validity period for its own imports.

question: Under the EU-UK TCA, for how long must the exporter keep a copy of the statement on origin and the supporting records?
expected: At least four years after the statement on origin was made out (Article 59(2)); the importer keeps its records at least three years after importation.
answer: Under the EU-UK TCA, the exporter must keep a copy of the statement on origin and the supporting records for at least three years as of the date of making out the statement on origin [04c8b496fb-0007]. The importer must keep a copy of the statement on origin or a copy thereof if the original is held by the customs authority or competent governmental authority for at least three years as of the date of importation of the product.

question: What is the general tolerance for non-originating materials in the EU-UK TCA for products outside Chapters 50 to 63?
expected: 10 % of the ex-works price of the product (Article 42(1)(b)); textiles follow Notes 7 and 8 of Annex 2.
answer: The general tolerance for non-originating materials in the EU-UK TCA for products outside Chapters 50 to 63 is 10% of the ex-works price of the product, as stated in Article 42 of the TCA [a7547bfef8-0006]. This tolerance applies to non-originating materials that do not meet the requirements set out in Annex 3-B of the TCA.

question: Under the EU-UK TCA, up to what value are small packages and travellers' personal luggage imported into the EU exempt from a statement on origin?
expected: EUR 500 for small packages and EUR 1 200 for personal luggage (Article 60(2)(b)(ii)); the UK sets its own limits.
answer: Under the EU-UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement (TCA), small consignments and travellers' personal luggage imported into the EU are exempt from the requirement for a statement on origin, provided their total value does not exceed EUR 500 for small packages or EUR 1,200 for products in travellers' personal luggage [4af5af7293-0015]. This exemption applies to goods not imported by way of trade and must be declared as meeting the requirements of the TCA. If the goods are not of EU origin, the exemption does not apply, and a statement on origin would be required [36b53d745c-0126].

question: UK customs is verifying our customer's preference claim and has asked the EU customs authorities for information about our goods. If 10 months pass without an answer from the EU side, what can happen?
expected: UK customs may deny preferential tariff treatment: Article 63(1)(c) allows it when, within 10 months of the request under Article 62(2), the exporting Party's customs authority has not replied or its reply does not confirm origin.
answer: If 10 months pass without an answer from the EU side, the requesting customs authorities may refuse entitlement to the preferences, as stated in Article 6 of the PEM rules [706bb77c4a-0056]. This applies unless exceptional circumstances are met. The EU customs authorities are required to inform the requesting customs authorities of the results of the verification as soon as possible, but no later than ten months following the request for verification [706bb77c4a-0056]. If the EU does not respond within this timeframe, the requesting customs authorities may deny the preferential treatment.

question: Does the EU-UK TCA prohibit duty drawback on non-originating materials?
expected: No. It only provides that, not earlier than two years after entry into force and at the request of either Party, the Trade Specialised Committee shall review the Parties' duty drawback and inward-processing schemes (Article 53): the review is mandatory once a Party asks for it.
answer: The EU-UK TCA does not prohibit duty drawback on non-originating materials. According to the passage [04c8b496fb-0042], the ITA (EU-Mercosur Interim Trade Agreement) does not contain a duty drawback prohibition provision, and the EU-UK TCA allows duty drawback for non-originating materials when the products acquire EU preferential origin. This applies to products under the inward processing procedure in the EU. Therefore, non-originating materials used in the manufacture of a product in the EU can be eligible for duty drawback when the products acquire EU preferential origin.

question: We sell a gift set to the UK made of EU-originating products plus one item bought from China. Can the whole set still count as originating under the TCA?
expected: Yes, if the value of the non-originating components does not exceed 15 % of the ex-works price of the set (Article 48).
answer:
Under the EU-UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement (TCA), a set is considered originating if all its components are originating or if the value of non-originating components does not exceed 15% of the ex-works price of the set. In this case, the gift set contains EU-originating products and one item from China. Since the non-originating component (the China item) has a value that does not exceed 15% of the ex-works price of the set, the entire set can still be considered originating under the TCA.  

This is supported by the TCA rules, specifically Article 48 and the guidance provided in the European Commission's document [3804f88053-0298] and [a7547bfef8-0013].  

Therefore, the whole set can still count as originating under the TCA.

question: We export plug-in hybrid and fully electric cars from the EU to the UK this year. What product-specific rule of origin do they have to meet under the TCA?
expected: MaxNOM 55 % (EXW): non-originating materials may not exceed 55 % of the ex-works price. This interim rule of Annex 5, Section 2 applies from 1 January 2024 until 31 December 2026; until the end of 2023 it was MaxNOM 60 %.
answer:
The EU-UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement (TCA) specifies that for vehicles equipped with an internal combustion engine, the value of non-originating materials may not exceed 45% of the ex-works price of the finished product. If the UK and/or European parts account for at least 55% of the final value, no customs duty applies when vehicles are exported to the EU [36b53d745c-0145]. For plug-in hybrid and electric cars, the rule of origin requires that battery blocks of heading 85.07 be originating, and the value of non-originating materials may not exceed 40% of the ex-works price for plug-in hybrids and 60% for electric cars [d31784ed8e-0003][d31784ed8e-0001]. 

The transitional rules for electric accumulators and electrified vehicles apply from 1 January 2024 until 31 December 2026, with specific limits on the maximum non-originating material value [d31784ed8e-0002].

question: We assemble EV battery packs in the EU from battery cells imported from Asia and sell them to the UK. Is the assembly enough for the packs to be EU originating under the TCA?
expected: No, assembly alone is no longer enough. Until 31 December 2026 the battery packs of 85.07 need a change of tariff heading, except from non-originating active cathode materials, or non-originating materials not exceeding 40 % of the ex-works price (Annex 5, Section 2). Assembling packs from non-originating cells only qualified until the end of 2023.
answer:
Under the EU-UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement, the transitional product-specific rules for electric accumulators and electrified vehicles apply until 31 December 2023. For battery packs, the rule requires that the battery cells or modules are sourced from the EU, with a maximum of 70% non-originating materials (EXW). If the assembly is done in the EU, it may qualify as EU originating under the TCA, provided the assembly meets the requirements of the transitional rules. 

For vehicles with both internal combustion engine and electric motor, the rules apply from 1 January 2024 until 31 December 2026. The assembly rule for battery packs changes to require that at least 40% of the materials are EU-originating, with a maximum of 50% non-originating materials (EXW). 

If the assembly is done in the EU, it may qualify as EU originating under the TCA, provided the assembly meets the requirements of the transitional rules.

question: For how long is a long-term supplier's declaration normally valid under the EU-UK TCA?
expected: Up to two years from the date it is made out; customs may allow longer periods (Annex 6, point 3).
answer: Under the EU-UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement, a long-term supplier’s declaration is normally valid for a period of up to two years from the date of making out the declaration [706bb77c4a-0046]. The customs authorities of the Party where the declaration is made out may allow longer periods under specific conditions. The declaration must be made in the form provided in Appendix 6-B and must describe the products in sufficient detail to identify them [706bb77c4a-0046]. The supplier must inform the customer immediately if the declaration ceases to apply to the products supplied [706bb77c4a-0046].

question: Which code goes in the EU customs declaration when a TCA preference claim is based on a statement on origin, and which one when it is based on importer's knowledge?
expected: U116 for a statement on origin, U117 for importer's knowledge, U118 for a statement covering multiple shipments of identical products.
answer: When a TCA preference claim is based on a statement on origin, the code to be used in the EU customs declaration is **U116** [4af5af7293-0012]. When the claim is based on importer’s knowledge, the code to be used is **U117** [4af5af7293-0012].

question: If an importer did not claim preference when importing goods under the EU-UK TCA, how long do they have to claim it retrospectively?
expected: Up to three years after the importation, on the basis of a statement on origin or of the importer's knowledge.
answer: If an importer did not claim preference when importing goods under the EU-UK TCA, they have up to three years after the date of importation to claim it retrospectively [36b53d745c-0059]. This period is specified in the EU-UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement and applies to cases where the importer has not claimed preferential treatment at the time of import. The retrospective claim can be based on a statement on origin or the importer’s own knowledge [4af5af7293-0012]. The Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2020/2254 of 29 December 2020 provides a transitory period for EU exporters to make statements on origin, which may allow the importer to claim preference at the moment of import [36b53d745c-0059]. The rules also allow for a retrospective claim up to three years after importation, provided the importer retains all necessary information to prove the product is of preferential origin [36b53d745c-0059].

question: Can EU goods sent to a distribution centre in the UK and then re-exported to the EU without processing benefit from preferential treatment?
expected: No: they have not obtained UK originating status. Transit or returned goods procedures may avoid the tariffs.
answer:
EU goods sent to a distribution centre in the UK and then re-exported to the EU without processing can benefit from preferential treatment under the EU-UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement (TCA) if they meet the requirements of the Product Specific Rule (PSR) for the product. However, if the goods are not originating from the UK, they may not qualify for preferential treatment in the EU. 

This is because the UK's withdrawal from the Single Market and Customs Union means that goods imported from the UK are subject to customs formalities and may be subject to tariffs. 

The rules of origin under the TCA apply to goods that have undergone processing in the UK, but if the goods are not processed in the UK, they may still qualify for preferential treatment if they meet the PSR requirements. 

It is important to note that the rules on trade in food products are stricter, and goods must undergo processing in the UK that goes beyond simple packaging to qualify for preferential treatment. 

The answer depends on whether the goods meet the PSR requirements and whether the processing in the UK meets the necessary criteria for preferential treatment.

question: Does a statement on origin under the EU-UK TCA have to be signed?
expected: No, a signature is not required.
answer:
Under the EU-UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement (TCA), a signature is not required in the declaration of origin for the purposes of the TCA [36b53d745c-0037]. The statement on origin can be made out on an invoice or any other document that describes the product in sufficient detail to identify it. The exporter is responsible for ensuring the information provided in the statement is correct and accurate [4af5af7293-0006]. 

If the UK customer cannot register for REX, the EU supplier can still issue a statement on origin if they are registered in REX for consignments of more than EUR 6000 [36b53d745c-0016]. The EU supplier is responsible for fulfilling the conditions of the origin chapter of the TCA. 

The statement on origin is made out by the exporter, and it is up to the exporter to ensure the information is correct and that the product is originating in the EU [4af5af7293-0006]. 

There is no requirement for a signature in the declaration of origin under the TCA [36b53d745c-0037].

question: May a TCA statement on origin indicate the origin with abbreviations such as EU, UE, UK or GB?
expected: Yes, in full or abbreviated; statements made out in the EU should not name individual Member States.
answer:
The TCA allows the origin of products to be indicated either in full or using abbreviations. For the EU, the origin may be indicated as "the Union," "European Union," "EU," or "UE." For the UK, the origin may be indicated as "the United Kingdom," "UK," or "GB." Abbreviations like "EU" or "UE" are acceptable for the EU, but "UK" or "GB" are acceptable for the UK.  

The TCA states that a statement on origin can be made out on any document that describes the originating product in sufficient detail to identify it. This includes invoices or other documents, and the exporter is responsible for ensuring the information is correct.  

If a UK exporter uses "United Kinkdom" as the country of origin, it is considered a minor typing error and is covered by Article 57 of the TCA, allowing preference to be granted in the EU. However, using "England" as the country of origin is not a minor error but an incorrect reference and is not covered by Article 57.  

The TCA does not allow the indication of individual Member States in the statement of origin. For the UK, only "the United Kingdom," "UK," or "GB" is acceptable. "GB" covers the entire UK, including Northern Ireland, so it is acceptable to use "GB" as a shorthand for the UK.

question: Do UK exporters need an EU REX number to make out statements on origin under the TCA?
expected: No. They use the reference number assigned under UK rules (the GB EORI number); the UK does not use REX.
answer:
The statement on origin for a UK exporter must include a reference number by which the exporter is identified, which is assigned according to the UK rules, specifically the GB EORI number. For EU exporters, the REX number is required for consignments exceeding EUR 6,000, but for consignments below this amount, no REX registration is necessary. UK exporters must include a GB EORI number in the statement on origin regardless of the consignment value. The EU-UK TCA does not require EU exporters to include an EORI number on the invoice, but they must include their REX number in the statement on origin for consignments over EUR 6,000. The REX system is used by EU exporters to verify their eligibility for preferential treatment under the TCA.

question: Which annex of the EU-UK TCA contains the text of the statement on origin, and is it the same as Annex ORIG-4?
expected: Annex 7. Annex ORIG-4 is the earlier numbering of the same annex, still used in the Commission's Q&A; the guide for traders writes 'Annex 7 TCA (ex-Annex ORIG-4)'.
answer:
The text of the statement on origin is contained in Annex ORIG-4 of the EU-UK TCA [36b53d745c-0037]. This is explicitly stated in the answer to Question 31. Annex ORIG-4 is the same as Annex ORIG-4, so there is no difference between them. 

Therefore, the answer is: The text of the statement on origin is in Annex ORIG-4 of the EU-UK TCA, and it is the same as Annex ORIG-4.

question: Under the EU-Japan EPA, up to what value are small packages imported into Japan admitted as originating without a statement on origin?
expected: 100,000 yen, or such amount as Japan may establish (Article 3.20(2)(b)); for the EU, EUR 500 and EUR 1,200.
answer:
Under the EU-Japan EPA, small packages imported into Japan are admitted as originating without a statement on origin provided they meet the following criteria:  
1. The total value does not exceed 100,000 yen [a5f860bda7-0025].  
2. The products are not imported by way of trade and have been declared as satisfying the requirements of the EPA [a5f860bda7-0025].  
3. There is no doubt as to the veracity of the declaration [a5f860bda7-0025].

question: What is the general tolerance for non-originating materials in the EU-Japan EPA?
expected: 10 % of the ex-works or free on board price of the product, for Chapters 1-49 and 64-97 (Article 3.6); textiles follow Notes 6 to 8 of Annex 3-A.
answer:
The general tolerance for non-originating materials in the EU-Japan EPA is 10% of the ex-works or free on board (FOB) price of the product, as stated in Article 3.6 of the agreement [a5f860bda7-0008]. This tolerance applies to products classified under Chapters 1 to 49 or Chapters 64 to 97 of the Harmonized System, unless the value of non-originating materials exceeds the 10% threshold [a5f860bda7-0008]. 

The EU-Japan EPA also allows for alternative calculations based on ex-works or FOB prices, as noted in Note 4 of the Introductory Notes to product specific rules of origin [3804f88053-0048].

question: Which origin criterion code must the exporter indicate on an EU-Japan statement on origin when the product is originating thanks to the tolerance?
expected: Code "E" (tolerance referred to in Article 3.6).
answer: The exporter must indicate the origin criterion code "A" or "B" or "C" depending on the specific product category, and for "A" or "B" it may include the code "1" if there is a change in tariff classification rule. The code "1" is used for a change in tariff classification rule, "2" for a maximum value of non-originating materials or a minimum regional value content rule, and "3" for a specific production process rule. The origin criterion code is indicated in the statement on origin as per the EU-Japan EPA guidance [4c45e9934a-0002].

question: Does a statement on origin under the EU-Japan EPA need a signature or a stamp?
expected: No, it does not need to be signed or stamped by the exporter or by any governmental authority.
answer: A statement on origin under the EU-Japan EPA does not need a signature or a stamp. The passage explicitly states that "A statement on origin does not need to be signed or stamped by the exporter or by any governmental authority" [4c45e9934a-0006].

question: Which reference number identifies a Japanese exporter on an EU-Japan statement on origin?
expected: The Japan Corporate Number.
answer: The reference number that identifies a Japanese exporter on an EU-Japan statement on origin is the Japan Corporate Number [4c45e9934a-0009]. This number is assigned by the National Tax Agency in Japan and is used to identify the exporter in the statement. If no number is assigned, the exporter's full address can be provided under the "Place and date" section [4c45e9934a-0009].

question: Under the EU-Japan EPA, what rule applies to cars of heading 87.03 from the seventh year after entry into force?
expected: MaxNOM 45 % (EXW) or RVC 60 % (FOB) (Appendix 3-B-1, Section 2); before it was 55/50 and 50/55.
answer: Under the EU-Japan Economic Partnership Agreement, for cars of heading 87.03, the rule applies from the beginning of the seventh year. Specifically, from the seventh year onward, the maximum NOM percentage is 45% (EXW) or RVC 60% (FOB). This is based on the provisions in Section 2 of Appendix 3-B-1 [0a83c985d6-0001].

question: A French winegrower uses bentonite imported from the US to clarify wine exported to Japan. Does the bentonite prevent the wine from being wholly obtained?
expected: No. It is filtered out and not present in the final product, so it is a neutral element (Article 3.13 of the EU-Japan EPA) and criterion A can be indicated.
answer: According to the EU-Japan EPA guidance, bentonite used in the production of wine and filtered out at the end of the process is considered a neutral element [3804f88053-0262]. This means it does not need to be taken into account when determining whether the wine was wholly obtained in the EU. Therefore, the bentonite does not prevent the wine from being considered as wholly obtained in the EU.

question: Under the EU-Korea FTA, up to what value can any exporter (not an approved exporter) make out an origin declaration?
expected: For consignments whose total value does not exceed 6000 euros (Article 16(1)(b)); above that, only approved exporters.
answer: Under the EU-Korea FTA, any exporter (not an approved exporter) can make an origin declaration if the total value of the consignment of originating products, based on the ex-works price, does not exceed EUR 6,000 [89c49ea6e4-0021]. This applies to both handwritten and typed declarations, with the text in Annex III of the origin protocol [89c49ea6e4-0021].

question: For how long must the exporter keep a copy of the origin declaration under the EU-Korea FTA?
expected: Five years (Article 23(1)).
answer: Under the EU-Korea FTA, the exporter must keep a copy of the origin declaration for five years [89c49ea6e4-0030]. This applies to both the origin declaration and the supporting documents referred to in Article 16.3. The records may include electronic records.

question: What is the value limit for small packages imported into Korea without a proof of origin?
expected: 1000 US dollars, for small packages and for travellers' personal luggage alike (Article 21(3)(b)).
answer: The value limit for small packages imported into Korea without a proof of origin is 500 euros. This is specified in Article 21 of the EU-Korea Free Trade Agreement Protocol on origin [89c49ea6e4-0027].

question: How must a handwritten origin declaration be written under the EU-Korea FTA?
expected: In ink, in capital characters (Article 16(4)).
answer: A handwritten origin declaration under the EU-Korea FTA must be written in ink in capital characters [89c49ea6e4-0022]. The declaration should be drawn up in accordance with the respective footnotes and the laws and regulations of the exporting Party [89c49ea6e4-0022]. If the statement on origin is handwritten, it shall be written in ink in printed characters [89c49ea6e4-0022]. The text of the origin declaration appears in Annex III of the origin protocol [89c49ea6e4-0021].

question: Korean customs doubts our origin declaration and has sent a verification request to the EU customs authorities. What happens to our customer's preference if no answer arrives within 10 months?
expected: Korean customs shall, except in exceptional circumstances, refuse the preference; the same applies if the reply is not sufficient to determine the authenticity of the declaration or the real origin of the products (Article 27(7)).
answer: If no answer arrives within 10 months of the verification request, the requesting customs authorities (in this case, EU customs authorities) may refuse entitlement to the preferential tariff treatment [13fbe87e43-0032]. The period of 10 months may be extended by mutual agreement, but if it is not, the preferential treatment is withheld.

question: Can an origin declaration under the EU-Korea FTA be made out after the goods have been exported?
expected: Yes, if it is presented in the importing Party no longer than two years (or the period in its legislation) after the importation (Article 16(6)).
answer: Under the EU-Korea FTA, an origin declaration may be made out after the goods have been exported, provided that the declaration is presented in the importing Party no longer than two years or the period specified in the legislation of the importing Party after the importation of the products [89c49ea6e4-0022]. The declaration must be made out by the exporter and must be in accordance with the legislation of the exporting Party [89c49ea6e4-0022].

question: How long is an origin declaration valid under CETA?
expected: 12 months from the date it was completed by the exporter, or longer if the Party of import provides so (Article 20).
answer: Under CETA, an origin declaration is valid for 12 months from the date it was completed by the exporter [dc1e68a1fd-0033]. If the declaration is submitted after the validity period, the importing Party may still accept it for preferential tariff treatment in accordance with its laws [dc1e68a1fd-0033]. The validity period may be extended by the importing Party if needed.

question: Under CETA, for how long must the exporter keep the origin declaration and supporting documents?
expected: Three years after completing the origin declaration, or longer if the Party of export specifies (Article 26(1)).
answer: Under CETA, the exporter must keep the origin declaration and supporting documents for three years after the completion of the origin declaration, as specified in Article 26, paragraph 1 [dc1e68a1fd-0040]. If the exporter based the origin declaration on a written statement from the producer, the producer must maintain records in accordance with paragraph 1 [dc1e68a1fd-0040].

question: What is the general tolerance for non-originating materials under CETA?
expected: 10 % of the transaction value or ex-works price of the product (Article 6(1)(a)).
answer: The general tolerance for non-originating materials under CETA is 10 per cent of the transaction value or ex-works price of the product, as stated in the Tolerance provisions of the Protocol [dc1e68a1fd-0011]. This tolerance allows manufacturers to use non-originating materials up to this percentage, but it cannot exceed the percentage specified in the product-specific rules [4af5af7293-0017]. For textile and apparel products, the tolerance is determined according to Annex 1 [dc1e68a1fd-0011].

question: We are a Canadian garment maker that sews shirts from fabric imported from China. Can the shirts be exported to the EU as originating under CETA?
expected: As a rule, no: CETA textiles and apparel follow double transformation, so sewing imported fabric is not enough. The exception is the limited, reciprocal origin quotas by product category (Annex 6), whose volumes are not in the corpus.
answer:
Under EU-Canada CETA, if cotton fabric is imported from China and processed in the EU to make tennis shoes, the fabric is considered non-originating, and the duties on the fabric are payable in the EU. However, if the fabric is cut and attached to originating soles in the EU, the tennis shoes are considered originating under CETA, and no duty is payable in the EU. This is because the EU-Canada CETA prohibits duty drawback, meaning the import duty on the non-originating fabric is payable in the EU. 

In contrast, under EU-UK TCA, if cotton yarn is imported from the USA and processed in the EU to make cotton fabric, the yarn is considered originating, and no duty is payable in the EU. This is because the EU-UK TCA does not prohibit duty drawback, allowing the use of non-originating materials in the production of originating products.

The rules of origin for textiles and apparel under CETA are based on the principle of double transformation, where the fabric must be transformed in the EU or UK to be considered originating. The use of non-originating materials is allowed under tolerances, provided they do not exceed certain thresholds.

question: Under the EU-Mercosur interim agreement, for how long must the exporter keep the statement on origin?
expected: At least 3 years from the date it was made out; the importer, at least 3 years from importation (Article 3.22).
answer: The exporter must keep the statement on origin for at least 3 years as of the date of making out the statement on origin [13fbe87e43-0027]. The importer must keep the statement on origin, or a copy thereof, for at least 3 years as of the date of importation of the products to which that statement on origin refers [13fbe87e43-0027].

question: Will the EU accept a 'certificate of origin' issued in a Mercosur country under the interim agreement, and for how long?
expected: Yes, as a transitional measure, for up to 3 years from entry into force, extendable by up to 2 years by notification (Annex 3-D).
answer: The EU accepts a 'certificate of origin' issued in a Mercosur country under the EU-Mercosur Interim Agreement on Trade, provided it meets the requirements set out in Annex 3-D ITA [04c8b496fb-0060]. This certificate is valid for a maximum period of five years from the date of entry into force of the Agreement [638fb4ef97-0005]. The certificate may be issued in English, Portuguese, or Spanish by authorized entities in Mercosur and must be completed in full, with the exception of optional boxes 5 (transport details) and 12 (observations) [04c8b496fb-0019]. The EU was informed of the choice made by each Mercosur signatory state regarding the statement on origin as of the provisional application of the Agreement (1 May 2026) [04c8b496fb-0060].

question: Does the EU-Mercosur interim agreement prohibit duty drawback?
expected: No. It has no drawback prohibition, so materials under inward processing can keep duties suspended when originating products are exported to Mercosur.
answer: The EU-Mercosur Interim Agreement does not prohibit duty drawback [04c8b496fb-0042]. If non-originating materials are used in the production of a product in the EU, those materials are eligible for duty drawback when the product acquires EU preferential origin. This applies to products under the inward processing procedure [04c8b496fb-0042]. The agreement allows for duty drawback in the context of the EU-UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement, but not in the EU-Mercosur agreement [4af5af7293-0019]. Therefore, duty drawback is permitted under the EU-Mercosur agreement.

question: Which reference number must Argentinian exporters show on a statement on origin under the EU-Mercosur agreement?
expected: Their CUIT (Clave única de identificación tributaria), an 11-digit tax number, whatever the value of the shipment, plus name and signature.
answer: Argentinian exporters under the EU-Mercosur agreement must include their Single Tax Identification Number (CUIT) as a reference number on a statement on origin. This is specified in the guidance provided in [04c8b496fb-0014]. The CUIT is a 11-digit number, such as 12345678901 or 20-00000000-3, and it must be included regardless of the value of the originating products.

question: From what date has the EU-Mercosur interim trade agreement been provisionally applied?
expected: From 1 May 2026.
answer: The EU-Mercosur Interim Trade Agreement (ITA) has been provisionally applied from 1 May 2026 [04c8b496fb-0002].

question: Can a Paraguayan exporter use the Annex 3-C statement on origin to obtain preferential treatment in the EU?
expected: No: for the time being Paraguay uses only the statement on origin in the form of a 'certificate' under Annex 3-D.
answer: A Paraguayan exporter cannot use the Annex 3-C statement on origin to obtain preferential treatment in the EU, as Paraguay has chosen to use only the "certificate" under Annex 3-D ITA for the time being. This means that the statement on origin as per the model in Annex 3-C ITA is not valid for preferential treatment in the EU during the transition period. [638fb4ef97-0003]

question: Which supporting document code is declared in the EU for a statement on origin under the EU-Mercosur agreement?
expected: U126 (with preference code 300, or 320 for quotas).
answer: The supporting document code declared in the EU for a statement on origin under the EU-Mercosur agreement is U126 Statement on origin [04c8b496fb-0004]. This code is specified in the D.E. type of supporting document 12 03 002 000, which outlines the requirements for statements on origin.

question: How long is a proof of origin valid under the revised PEM Convention?
expected: Ten months from the date of issue or making out in the exporting Contracting Party (Article 23).
answer: Under the revised PEM Convention, a proof of origin is valid for ten months from the date of issue or making out in the exporting Contracting Party [706bb77c4a-0040]. If submitted after this period, it may still be accepted for tariff preferences if the failure to submit was due to exceptional circumstances [706bb77c4a-0040]. Additionally, proofs of origin issued before the end of the transition period, such as those from the UK, are considered valid for Article 23(1) of Appendix I of the PEM Convention if imported into an EU partner country after the transition period [36b53d745c-0133].

question: What is the value tolerance for non-originating materials under the revised PEM rules for industrial products?
expected: 15 % of the ex-works price (Article 5); for Chapters 2 and 4-24, 15 % of the net weight.
answer:
Under the revised PEM rules, the value tolerance for non-originating materials for industrial products is 10% of the ex-works price of the product. This is specified in the Revised PEM Convention, which sets a 15% tolerance for all products except those in HS Chapters 50 to 63. However, for industrial products, the 10% value tolerance applies, which may be combined with other tolerances as permitted by the rules.

question: Does the revised PEM Convention prohibit duty drawback?
expected: Only for non-originating materials used in products of Chapters 50 to 63 (textiles), with exceptions for certain cumulation and bilateral trade (Article 16).
answer: The prohibition of duty drawback applies to duties on non-originating goods when they are put into free circulation, and it covers customs duties, antidumping duties, safeguard measures, and other charges having equivalent effect, except where otherwise indicated in the respective agreement [3804f88053-0281]. Under the PEM Convention, the prohibition of duty drawback applies to materials used in the production of products exported under preference, and the exporter must submit documents proving that no drawback has been obtained [706bb77c4a-0028]. The EU-UK TCA allows duty drawback for at least the first two years of application, but after that, it may be reviewed by the Trade Specialised Committee on Customs Cooperation and Rules of Origin [36b53d745c-0153]. The PEM Transitional rules provide guidance on the application of the prohibition of duty drawback in the Pan-Euro-Mediterranean zone [3804f88053-0281].

question: Which proofs of origin does the revised PEM Convention provide for?
expected: The movement certificate EUR.1 and the origin declaration on an invoice or other commercial document (Article 17); parties may agree on statements by registered exporters.
answer: The revised PEM Convention provides for proofs of origin including the movement certificate EUR.1 and the origin declaration [706bb77c4a-0055]. The verification of these proofs is required under Article 34 [706bb77c4a-0055], and discrepancies or formal errors are addressed under Article 28 [706bb77c4a-0055]. The validity of proofs of origin is limited to the period established under the relevant EU trade preferential arrangements [36b53d745c-0133].

question: Our factory exports to Korea and to Brazil and makes out the origin declarations itself. How long do we have to keep them and their supporting documents for each market?
expected: Korea: five years (Article 23 of the Korea protocol). Brazil, under the EU-Mercosur agreement: at least three years from the date the statement was made out (Article 3.22).
answer: For Korea, the exporter must keep the origin declaration and supporting documents for five years [89c49ea6e4-0030]. For Brazil, the exporter must keep the origin declaration and supporting documents for three years [04c8b496fb-0007]. The importer in both cases must keep the origin declaration and supporting documents for three years [04c8b496fb-0007]. The customs authorities in both cases must keep the origin declarations submitted to them for five years [89c49ea6e4-0030]. The exporter must keep the origin declaration and supporting documents for at least three years from the date of making out the origin declaration, unless a longer period is specified by the importing Party [706bb77c4a-0050].

question: When is a pick-up type multipurpose vehicle classified in heading 8704 instead of 8703?
expected: When the maximum inner length at the floor of the goods area is more than 50 % of the wheelbase, or when it has more than two axles.
answer:
A pick-up type multipurpose vehicle is classified in heading 8704 instead of 8703 if the maximum inner length at the floor of the area for the transport of the goods is more than 50% of the length of the wheelbase of the vehicle or if the vehicle has more than two axles [2f02ea227e-0010]. 

This classification rule applies to vehicles that are not classified in heading 8703 due to the specific criteria mentioned [2f02ea227e-0010].

question: ¿Caduca el número REX de un exportador registrado?
expected: No, su validez no está limitada en el tiempo, salvo revocación.
answer: El número REX de un exportador registrado no está limitado en el tiempo [3ac8ead017-0022]. Si se revoca el registro, las autoridades competentes establecen una fecha a partir de la cual la revocación surtirá efecto, limitando así la validez del número REX hasta esa fecha [3ac8ead017-0022]. La validez del número REX se mantiene hasta que se revoca el registro o se cumpla con los requisitos para su revocación.

question: ¿Qué estructura tiene un número REX?
expected: Código ISO del país (2 letras), «REX» (3 letras) y una cadena de hasta 30 caracteres alfanuméricos.
answer: El número REX tiene una estructura específica que incluye un identificador único asignado al exportador registrado. Este número se utiliza para certificar el origen de las mercancías exportadas en el contexto de acuerdos comerciales preferenciales [3ac8ead017-0006]. El número REX no está limitado en el tiempo y se puede utilizar en todos los acuerdos comerciales preferenciales en los que el sistema de certificación de origen aplicado sea el sistema REX [3ac8ead017-0022]. La validez del número REX no se limita a un período específico [3ac8ead017-0022].

question: Si me revocan el registro REX y vuelvo a registrarme, ¿recupero mi antiguo número?
expected: No: se asigna un número nuevo y no se reutiliza el revocado, salvo que la revocación se anule.
answer:
Si me revocan el registro REX y vuelvo a registrarme, el antiguo número de registro no se reutilizará [6]. Las autoridades competentes asignarán un nuevo número de registro al exportador y no reutilizarán el antiguo número de registro revocado, excepto en el caso de anulación de la revocación [6]. 

La validez del número de registro no está limitada en el tiempo, pero la revocación implica que el número de registro pierde su validez y no se puede utilizar para nuevos registros [3ac8ead017-0022]. 

En la UE, el número de registro revocado no debe utilizarse para nuevos registros de exportadores [3ac8ead017-0025]. 

Por lo tanto, si se revoca el registro REX, el antiguo número no se recupera y se asigna un nuevo número de registro.
